The benchmark stock index, already the world39;s worst performer this year, plunged 11 to a sixyear low, while the rupiah slid 0.6 to 18,070 per US dollar, its weakest level since late July. Indonesian equities have struggled since January when MSCI froze Indonesia in its indexes and threatened a downgrade to frontier status because of opacity in ownership and trading behaviour. On Friday, MSCI said reforms to address those problems have not made sufficient progress and that even a downgrade to frontier wouldn39;t reflect the severity of issues. Significant concerns remain around market dysfunction, MSCI said. Accordingly, MSCI considers Indonesia39;s continued classification as an emerging market no longer appropriate, it said in a statement.
